extracted.intended_audience: institutional investors, Vanguard fund shareholders, and portfolio company executives/boards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards Vanguard’s Investment Stewardship team uses to assess portfolio-company governance and to inform proxy voting and engagement activities across regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek to understand to what extent board members ... are suitably independent, capable, and experienced to carry out their duties. We also aim to understand how boards assess and enhance their own effectiveness over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate independence, capability, relevant skills and experience, use of board evaluations and skills matrices, committee structure, and disclosures linking director attributes to company strategy. Consider regional norms (e.g., slate voting in Italy, comply-or-explain rules in U.K.) and vote against directors when disclosure is insufficient to assess independence or effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board refreshment processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards should leverage annual board evaluations and other processes to prioritize refreshment activities and recruit directors to close skills gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence that evaluations inform committee-structure changes and recruiting (e.g., hiring for AI, cybersecurity, public policy, global trade). Favor boards that link director skills to strategy and actively manage refreshment rather than only responding to activist pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board skills disclosure / skills matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear articulation of the individual skills and experience of board members, often linked to the company’s stated strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize disclosure of skills matrices and explanations of how nominees fit the desired board profile; interviews or disclosures from independent directors are helpful. Use these disclosures to assess whether the board is positioned to oversee strategy and material risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director independence assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the independence of director nominees and the adequacy of disclosures to allow that assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In markets with limited disclosure, engage companies seeking additional information. Vote against directors when disclosures are insufficient to assess independence or when independence requirements are not met under local law or best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair tenure and tenure-related governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards should consider chair tenure limits and associated governance guidance (e.g., the U.K. Corporate Governance Code guidance on chair tenure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comply-or-explain disclosures when tenure limits are exceeded; consider continuity needs during transitions versus independence concerns from long tenure. Use local codes (e.g., UK nine-year guidance, German cooling-off recommendation) to inform votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director capacity and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether directors have adequate capacity and time commitments to fulfill their duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider outside commitments and evidence of director engagement; where concerns about capacity or over-commitment arise, this can inform votes against nominees. Engage with companies to understand nominee time availability and other responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition and independent committee chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether key committees (audit, nomination, remuneration) are appropriately constituted and led, including by independent chairs where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for independent oversight of critical functions; support actions to appoint independent committee chairs and assess committee effectiveness as part of board evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive succession planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive succession should be treated as a continuous strategic priority with robust talent pipelines rather than a contingency plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek disclosure on succession planning, onboarding, transitional overlaps, and how boards oversee CEO and senior leadership succession. Favor boards increasing transparency about these processes in proxy statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board oversight of strategy and material risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards should actively oversee company strategy and material risks (e.g., AI, cybersecurity, regulatory change, tariffs) and how risks present both threats and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate board processes, disclosures, and examples of oversight (scenario planning, workforce planning, supply-chain resilience). Favor boards that demonstrate oversight capability and that connect risk oversight to strategic decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure quality on material risks and regulatory reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Company disclosure should clearly explain material risks and how the board oversees them, including compliance with relevant reporting standards (e.g., CSRD, TCFD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the adequacy and clarity of disclosures, including double materiality reporting under CSRD, TCFD-aligned climate disclosures, and how disclosures support investor assessment of board oversight and financial materiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological risk oversight (AI and cybersecurity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards should identify technological risks (generative AI, cybersecurity) as material and ensure director education and preparedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of director upskilling, deep-dive sessions with management, preparedness exercises, external expert engagement, and specific board-level oversight activities to mitigate cyber and AI risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of shareholder proposals — case-by-case analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Shareholder proposals are considered on a case-by-case basis, assessing whether they are aligned with company strategy, justified by financial materiality, or fill a gap in practice/disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not support overly prescriptive proposals that direct operations or micromanage management. Consider SEC no-action trends, withdrawals after engagement, and whether the proposal addresses a demonstrable gap or financial-material concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Say on Climate and other 'Say on…' proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The funds evaluate Say on Climate proposals with focus on financial materiality, board oversight, and disclosure quality; 2025 policy clarified a general approach of abstaining on Say on Climate resolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether proposals provide sufficient disclosure of financial materiality and board oversight. Where the proposal or disclosures are unclear or the board is well-positioned to oversee climate risk, abstention or non-support may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive pay alignment with shareholder returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how a company’s executive pay program aligns pay outcomes with shareholder returns relative to a relevant set of industry peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review disclosure on board oversight of pay, plan structure, metrics, performance targets, and peer-group selection. Support remuneration when structure and disclosure demonstrate alignment with long-term shareholder returns; oppose when alignment is lacking or disclosure inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer benchmarking transparency in remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality and transparency of peer benchmarking exercises used to justify pay changes must be sufficient to justify pay increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor detailed peer-group analysis and transparent methodologies. Oppose remuneration policies when benchmarking is opaque, lacks rationale, or when increases are not supported by demonstrable alignment with shareholder interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time retention equity awards — disclosure and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards that grant one-time retention equity (or one-time awards) should provide clear rationale and contextual disclosure of facts and circumstances underlying the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage to request clarity on rationale (e.g., prevent attrition, re-engage employees, replace lost equity value). Expect measurable performance conditions and appropriate structure; oppose awards issued at significant discounts or with minimal/no performance conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for equity over cash awards
rubrics_metrics.description: When executives are awarded one-time awards, equity is generally preferred over cash because equity better aligns executive pay with shareholder returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge 'false choice' scenarios where companies claim cash will replace equity if equity is not approved. Emphasize governance structures that preserve shareholder voting rights and alignment incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of executive remuneration as standalone resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive remuneration should be presented as a standalone resolution with comprehensive disclosure of pay structure and measurable performance targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for standalone binding votes where jurisdiction permits, and for clear disclosure enabling assessment of variable pay awards and how metrics quantify performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareholder rights — preserving effective exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Support governance practices that preserve shareholders’ ability to exercise rights effectively (voting, proposals, meetings, protections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals that affect shareholder rights (listing changes, multiple-class shares, voting thresholds, rights to call special meetings) by assessing whether changes improve or weaken shareholder protections and governance safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redomestication / reincorporation proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate proposals to change a company’s state of incorporation on a case-by-case basis, considering rationale and impacts on regulatory, governance, and shareholder rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support when the new jurisdiction provides comparable or improved governance standards or when a compelling operational rationale exists; oppose when reincorporation would weaken shareholder protections or lacks compelling rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special meeting rights and continuous ownership thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the ownership thresholds and holding-period requirements for shareholders to call special meetings and the potential effect on shareholder voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether thresholds are reasonable given context (e.g., one-year holding period may not be excessive); evaluate whether elimination or modification would better enable shareholder rights without enabling opportunistic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supermajority voting requirements — narrow tailoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether existing supermajority voting standards are narrowly tailored and whether removing them would be beneficial to shareholder interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where supermajority provisions are narrowly applied to protect minority shareholders (e.g., limited transaction types), retaining them may be appropriate. Vote case-by-case rather than blanket support for elimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poison pills and takeover defenses — shareholder approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of takeover defenses (poison pills) without shareholder approval prevents assessment of their appropriateness and can entrench management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a company adopts a poison pill without a shareholder vote, consider voting against responsible directors; favor seeking shareholder approval before adopting significant takeover defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylaw amendments affecting shareholder proposal thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate proposed bylaw changes that alter thresholds for shareholders to submit proposals, focusing on effects to shareholder rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppose increases that would unduly restrict shareholders’ ability to submit proposals; support amended thresholds when, after engagement, they are assessed to adequately maintain shareholders’ rights and align with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional context and differentiated expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Governance practices and disclosure expectations vary across regions; engagement and voting decisions should reflect local market norms and regulatory regimes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In less-developed governance markets, prioritize encouraging disclosures and independence; in developed markets focus on nuanced issues (global pay benchmarking, CSRD, board diversity codes). Use regional briefs and local codes to inform assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement as mechanism to inform votes
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with company leaders and independent directors to understand rationale, gather additional disclosures, and encourage governance improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use engagement outcomes to influence vote decisions (e.g., proposals withdrawn after engagement). Expect boards to provide additional context; adjust support/oppose/abstain decisions based on engagement findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case evaluation approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the funds’ proxy voting policies on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the facts and circumstances at each company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid one-size-fits-all voting; weigh disclosures, engagement outcomes, local law, financial materiality, and likely effects on long-term shareholder returns when deciding votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of governance changes that may entrench management
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate proposals (e.g., removing board size limits, multiple-class shares, supermajority removal) for potential entrenchment risks versus stated governance or operational benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed changes lack mitigating governance measures and could enable entrenchment or dilute shareholder influence, consider voting against. Favor proposals that include safeguards for minority shareholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for management proposals aligned with long-term returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Support management proposals (such as capital allocation) when assessed to be aligned with long-term shareholder returns and consistent with governance best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate alignment with strategy, absence of misconduct, and board oversight; support management where these conditions are met and disclosures are adequate.
